Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign (codenamed "Nexion") of the real Nxeon VPS hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real database, real code paths, but no VM is ever actually provisioned and no card is ever actually charged). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST — it has non-negotiable rules for this tree, the most important one for you being: "Never fabricate. No invented stats, ratings, or capabilities. If a number/capability cannot be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why." This rule is central to your task — read it carefully before writing any code. Also skim docs/NEXION-V2.md if you want more design-direction context. Typecheck with `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit`.

You are ONE of 4 parallel background agents each fixing a different, non-overlapping part of this codebase's ongoing light/dark theme + redesign pass. COORDINATION RULE: do not run ./rebuild.sh or restart the nxeon-v2-web systemd service except when you genuinely need to see your own work render (reasonable to do a few times given the scope of this task), and do NOT create git commits — the orchestrating session will do one final integration rebuild + commit across all 4 agents' work when everyone is done.

BACKGROUND YOU NEED: this session already fully rebuilt the VPS server-management panel (components/customer/vpspanel/v2/*) with a new "liquid glass" visual language — read components/customer/vpspanel/v2/kit.tsx (esp. the `Panel`, `StatusPill`, `Metric`, `Segmented`, `CopyChip` components — `Panel` renders `card card-glass` with a `--tone` CSS custom property, which is the established reusable surface for this whole redesign) and components/customer/vpspanel/v2/ui.tsx (`SubNav`, `Card`) to understand the visual vocabulary you should match. This session ALSO just finished a large pass making the whole dashboard work correctly in a new LIGHT theme (dark was the only mode before; light is now a real, independent theme, toggled via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens defined as CSS custom properties `--color-*` in app/globals.css) — the single most important lesson from that pass, which you must apply from the start rather than retrofit later: NEVER hardcode a literal color (a raw hex or rgba like `bg-[rgba(10,22,48,.5)]`) for anything that should look different/legible in both light and dark mode — always use the existing `--color-*` tokens (`text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, etc. — grep app/globals.css for the full list) or the `card`/`card-glass` classes, which already adapt automatically. Only use a literal hardcoded color for something that is GENUINELY meant to look the same regardless of theme (e.g. a small saturated accent badge), and even then, if it sits on a page background rather than its own fixed artwork, wrap it in the `.nx-dark-island` class (also in app/globals.css) if it must stay permanently dark. If you're unsure, prefer tokens.

YOUR TASK — the user's own words, verbatim: "We also need to completely redo the upgrade resources and addons section. A interactive storage volume slider, similar to the storage addon from the deploy wizard (incorporate the same png icon asset we used there as well). For the plans, incorporate a small plan chart for the service, obviously they cannot downgrade their plan, so their current plan and plans underneath need to be grayed out with only the plans above it being pickable. If they are already on the max plan, there should also be an option (need more resources, contact support for a custom plan). I want there to also be a animated card that gets adjusted based off their selected upgrades, and as soon as they start interacting with addons and upgrades, the sticky cart card from deploy wizard slides up from the bottom with a smooth transition with all the addons and upgrades, and the checkout button pulls up a payment popup on screen with an option to pay credit card, or wallet balance. also somewhere there we need to have a addons card, maybe underneath the storage card with all the addons we support. If if they already have an addon it has to be greyed out. all of these affect the total renewal cost for the service. you need to completely start fresh with the design and structure of the resources tab because its very ugly on lightmode and darkmode."

This is the "Resources" tab of the VPS server management panel (visible as one of the 8 tabs — Overview/Console/Files/Services/Backups/Networking/Activity/Settings — under Settings, or possibly its own top-level tab; check components/customer/vpspanel/v2/VpsPanelShell.tsx for how it's wired in) — the entry point component is components/customer/vpspanel/v2/VpsResourcesPanel.tsx, which currently renders a header+3-tab-switcher (Plan/Storage/Network) and receives `planSlider`/`storageControl`/`networkControl` as props from its parent (find and read that parent to see current wiring — likely somewhere under app/dashboard/servers/[id]/ or similar). The plan slider itself is components/customer/vpspanel/v2/VpsPlanSlider.tsx.

CONCRETE FACTS ALREADY ESTABLISHED (verified by the orchestrating session before dispatching you, so you don't need to re-derive them, though you should verify anything load-bearing yourself):

1. PLAN SLIDER BUG: VpsPlanSlider.tsx already correctly PREVENTS downgrades functionally — the `selectable` variable (around line 77) already requires `target.priceCents > current.priceCents`. But the per-plan stop buttons rendered below the track (~lines 156-180) only visually dim (`opacity-40`) a plan when `tooSmall(p)` is true (disk would shrink) — they do NOT dim a plan that is simply at-or-below the current price tier, so right now every plan at or below the current one LOOKS fully pickable even though clicking "Apply" on one just shows an explanatory "ask support" message. Fix: also visually greyed-out/disabled-looking for any plan at index <= the current plan's index (not just disk-too-small ones), matching the user's explicit ask ("current plan and plans underneath need to be grayed out with only the plans above it being pickable").

2. MAX-PLAN STATE: there is currently an always-visible "Need something else? / Ask for a custom plan" card in the VpsResourcesPanel.tsx sidebar (unconditional, every server, every plan). The user wants an additional, MORE PROMINENT contact-support option specifically inline in the plan picker when the account is already on the top plan (i.e. `currentIdx === ordered.length - 1`) — add this alongside (not replacing) the existing sidebar card.

3. STORAGE SLIDER: the user wants it to look and feel like the existing "Extra storage" control already used elsewhere for the SAME real backend action — read components/customer/AddStorage.tsx FULLY first: it already implements the real logic (proration via `lib/extra-disk.ts`'s `extraDiskProrateCents`/`extraDiskCentsAt`/`maxAddableExtraDiskGB`/`effectiveDiskGB`, wallet/card split via `lib/wallet-split.ts`, and calls the real server action `expandServerDisk` from `lib/actions-disk.ts`, then opens `components/customer/StripeCheckoutModal.tsx` for the card portion) — it just has the OLD (pre-redesign) visual style, a plain range input with GB shortcut buttons. The user separately wants this to look like the interactive DiskMeter control already used in the DEPLOY WIZARD at components/nx/OrderBits.tsx (`DiskMeter` function, near the bottom of that file) — same visual treatment (the `/nx/svc/volume.webp` icon asset, a styled range slider, live GB/price readout) but wired to the REAL post-deploy logic from AddStorage.tsx (a fresh deploy's DiskMeter has no proration/wallet-split concerns since nothing is billed yet; this one does, and must keep AddStorage's real money math intact — do not re-derive or approximate it, reuse the actual functions).

4. ADDONS: this is the part you must be MOST careful not to fabricate. Search the codebase (`grep -rn "addon" lib/ components/customer/`) — you will find that there is NO generic "VPS addon catalog" in this codebase. The only things that already exist as REAL, separately-purchasable-after-deployment upgrades for a running VPS are: (a) extra storage (covered above) and (b) a dedicated IP, via `purchaseDedicatedIp` in lib/actions-dedicated-ip.ts, with an existing reference UI at components/customer/AddDedicatedIp.tsx (same money-math pattern as AddStorage.tsx: `extraDiskProrateCents` reused generically, `walletSplit`, `StripeCheckoutModal`). There ARE three boolean "addons" (malware scanner, daily backup, docker) but grep confirms these are DEPLOY-TIME-ONLY choices baked into the order at creation (lib/order.ts) — there is no backend action to add/change them after a server already exists. Given this, your "addons card" must legitimately offer ONLY what has a real backend action — realistically just Dedicated IP for now. If the server already has one (check whatever prop/field AddDedicatedIp.tsx already reads to decide whether to render at all — it says "Only rendered when the server doesn't already have one"), show it in the addons card as owned/greyed-out rather than hiding it entirely, per the user's explicit ask ("If they already have an addon it has to be greyed out"). Do NOT invent a "malware scanner" or "backup tier" purchase button — that capability does not exist on the backend, and adding a UI for it would be exactly the kind of fabrication CLAUDE.md forbids. If you find you were wrong and a real backend path DOES exist for another addon, use it — just verify first, don't assume.

5. STICKY CART BAR: the user wants "the sticky cart card from deploy wizard" reused. That's the sticky bottom summary bar in components/nx/DeployView.tsx (search for its `nx-dark-island` sticky bar, added earlier this session — read it for the visual pattern: fixed to the bottom of the viewport, dark surface, slides in). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE: DeployView's cart is for a single up-front purchase with ONE checkout at the end. Here, plan-resize / storage-expand / dedicated-IP-add are today THREE SEPARATE, ALREADY-WORKING, independent server actions and Stripe checkouts (resizeServer, expandServerDisk, purchaseDedicatedIp — each returns its own `{clientSecret, publishableKey}` and opens its own StripeCheckoutModal). Before building a unified cart+checkout UI, investigate whether the backend has (or should get) a way to combine multiple pending changes into ONE PaymentIntent/checkout. If it doesn't, you have two honest options: (a) scope-appropriate for this task — build a small new server action that combines the currently-selected pending changes (plan target, storage delta, dedicated-IP toggle) into one proration total and one Stripe PaymentIntent, mirroring the existing money-math functions (`prorateUpgradeCents`, `extraDiskProrateCents`, `walletSplit`) rather than reinventing them, then have the three existing actions become internal implementation details called after payment succeeds (or refactor the charge to be genuinely combined — your call based on what you find in lib/actions-server.ts, lib/actions-disk.ts, lib/actions-dedicated-ip.ts, and how their Stripe PaymentIntents/webhooks are reconciled); or (b) if combining the charge is out of scope or too risky to get right, build the CART UI to clearly show all pending changes and their combined total for the customer's understanding, but be transparent in the implementation (and in your final report) that "Checkout" processes them as sequential confirmations against the existing three actions rather than one PaymentIntent — never present a fake single combined charge if the backend doesn't actually do that. Whichever you choose, the popup itself should offer "pay by card" vs "pay by wallet balance" as the user asked — reuse the existing `walletSplit`/wallet-checkbox pattern already used in VpsPlanSlider.tsx/AddStorage.tsx/AddDedicatedIp.tsx (a checkbox to apply balance, remaining goes to card) rather than a from-scratch payment-method picker.

6. ANIMATED SUMMARY CARD: a card that shows the combined effect of everything currently selected (target plan if changed, storage GB to add if any, dedicated IP if toggled on) and the resulting price/renewal total, updating live as the customer adjusts controls, with a simple, tasteful transition on value changes (this codebase already has a `.num` class used everywhere for monospace figures — a plain CSS transition or the `nx-rise`/`nx-pop` animation classes already in app/globals.css are consistent with the rest of the redesign; no new animation library).

7. VISUAL REBUILD: VpsResourcesPanel.tsx's current header and tab-switcher use hardcoded literal dark gradients (`bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(10,22,48,.5),rgba(2,7,20,.62))]`, `bg-[rgba(4,10,28,.6)]`) that don't adapt to light theme at all — per the user ("very ugly on lightmode and darkmode... completely start fresh"), rebuild this using the established `card`/`card-glass`/token vocabulary from kit.tsx instead of literal colors, and feel free to restructure the whole tab's layout/composition (it does not need to preserve the current 3-tab Plan/Storage/Network switcher shape if a single scrolling column of cards — hero/plan card, storage card, addons card, sticky cart, usage rail — reads better; use your judgment, but keep whatever the parent component currently passes in as props/wiring working, or update the parent's wiring cleanly if you change the shape).

Work through this thoroughly — this is intentionally the largest of the 4 parallel tasks and is expected to take real time and touch several files (VpsResourcesPanel.tsx, VpsPlanSlider.tsx, likely a new storage-slider component, a new addons-card component, a new sticky-cart component, possibly a new combined-checkout server action, and the parent component that wires it all together). Iterate with `npx tsc --noEmit` as you go, and do at least one real rebuild + logged-in screenshot pass (see scripts/shot.mjs for the login flow) in both light and dark mode before declaring done — this whole task exists because the current version looks bad in both themes, so seeing it rendered matters more here than for a small CSS fix.

CONSTRAINTS: stay within components/customer/vpspanel/v2/*, the parent component that wires VpsResourcesPanel's props (find and read it), and lib/ files only if you're building the combined-checkout action described in point 5 (name it clearly, keep it additive — do not modify the existing resizeServer/expandServerDisk/purchaseDedicatedIp signatures in ways that could break other callers; check what else calls them first). Do not touch the Aurora/backdrop canvas files, components/nx/DeployView.tsx (read-only reference only), components/nx/RewardsView.tsx, or app/dashboard/services/* — those are owned by other parallel agents.

Write a thorough final report: what you built, which pieces map to which real backend action, exactly how you resolved the "combined checkout" question in point 5 and why, and any capability gap you found but chose not to build (e.g. if you decided sequential-checkout was the honest answer rather than a combined PaymentIntent) so the user can decide whether it's worth a bigger backend change later.

The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. 46 47 ## The tree 48 49 | | | 50 |---|---| 51 | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | 52 | Branch | `design/v2` | 53 | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | 54 | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | 55 | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | 56 | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | 57 | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | 58 59 `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and 60 it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` 61 builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. 62 63 Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node 64 and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing 65 to the other. 66 67 ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here 68 69 node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because 70 three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept 71 attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the 72 production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox 73 seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. 74 75 Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two 76 levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: 77 78 ```bash 79 scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title 80 scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments 81 scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ 82 scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD 83 scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else 84 ``` 85 86 **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production 87 database and the mail server. 1	/**
2	 * Per-server extra disk — pure, dependency-free maths + copy.
3	 *
4	 * Deliberately has NO server-only imports (no db, no settings) so the exact same
5	 * module can be imported by client components (DeployWizard, AddStorage) and by
6	 * the server actions / worker. Whatever the customer SEES is byte-for-byte what
7	 * gets CHARGED — mirroring lib/wallet-split.ts.
8	 *
9	 * This is the server's OWN root disk growing, which is a different product from
10	 * block-storage volumes (lib/actions-volumes.ts): a volume is portable and can be
11	 * detached and deleted; this space is fused into the VM's root filesystem.
12	 *
13	 * ─── GROWTH IS ONE-WAY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	 * A live filesystem cannot be shrunk without risking data loss, and no serious
15	 * provider offers it. There is NO shrink path anywhere in the platform, and
16	 * `Server.extraDiskGB` is never decremented. Every surface that sells extra
17	 * storage must show EXTRA_DISK_ONE_WAY_NOTE before taking the money.
18	 */
19	
20	/** Storage is sold in 10 GB increments — matches the slider/step in both UIs. */
21	export const EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB = 10;
22	/** Smallest purchasable amount. */
23	export const EXTRA_DISK_MIN_GB = 10;
24	/** Largest amount purchasable in a SINGLE transaction. */
25	export const EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB = 500;
26	/** Hard ceiling on a server's effective disk (plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB). */
27	export const EXTRA_DISK_MAX_TOTAL_GB = 2000;
28	/**
29	 * Fallback price per GB per month when the `extra_disk_gb_price_cents` admin
30	 * setting has never been written. 10 = $0.10/GB/mo, matching block storage.
31	 * Use `extraDiskMonthlyCents()` (lib/disk-expand.ts) in billing paths, never this.
32	 */
33	export const EXTRA_DISK_DEFAULT_PER_GB_CENTS = 10;
34	
35	/** The one-way warning, shown verbatim on every surface that sells extra disk. */
36	export const EXTRA_DISK_ONE_WAY_NOTE =
37	  "Storage can only be added, never removed. Extra disk space is permanent for this server's lifetime and keeps billing every cycle.";
38	
39	/** A server's EFFECTIVE root disk in GB — plan allowance plus purchased extra. */
40	export function effectiveDiskGB(planDiskGB: number, extraDiskGB: number | null | undefined): number {
41	  return Math.max(0, Math.round(planDiskGB)) + Math.max(0, Math.round(extraDiskGB ?? 0));
42	}
43	
44	/**
45	 * A server's BASE disk allowance (before extra-disk add-ons) — the game plan's
46	 * disk when the server has one, else the base VPS plan's. worker/index.ts's
47	 * `provision()` has provisioned every game server's REAL disk this way since
48	 * the 2026-09-06 over-provisioning fix (a game plan's disk is never larger
49	 * than its base VPS tier's), so `server.plan.diskGB` alone is the WRONG,
50	 * larger number for any game server — every caller of `effectiveDiskGB` that
51	 * takes a real `Server` row (not a bare `Plan`) must resolve through this
52	 * first, not pass `server.plan.diskGB` directly.
53	 *
54	 * Found live 2026-09-09 repeated across at least a dozen call sites (customer
55	 * dashboard, admin dashboard, disk-usage API, resize/reinstall validation,
56	 * disk-expand, capacity aggregates, the AI support-chat context, and the
57	 * disk-full monitor) — every one had independently reinvented
58	 * `server.plan.diskGB` instead of going through one shared helper, which is
59	 * exactly how the same bug kept reappearing one file at a time. This is that
60	 * one shared helper; new code must use it, not read `.plan.diskGB` directly
61	 * off a Server row.
62	 */
63	export function baseDiskGBFor(server: { plan: { diskGB: number }; gamePlan?: { diskGB: number } | null }): number {
64	  return server.gamePlan?.diskGB ?? server.plan.diskGB;
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * Monthly cost (integer cents) of `gb` extra GB at `perGbCents`. Exact integer
69	 * multiplication — no floating-point money.
70	 */
71	export function extraDiskCentsAt(gb: number, perGbCents: number): number {
72	  const g = Math.max(0, Math.round(gb));
73	  const p = Math.max(0, Math.round(perGbCents));
74	  return g * p;
75	}
76	
77	/**
78	 * The one-off charge for `monthlyCents` of extra disk over the months still left
79	 * on the current paid term. THE single definition, shared by the server
80	 * (lib/disk-expand.ts diskExpandQuote) and the control that DISPLAYS the figure
81	 * before the customer agrees to it (components/customer/AddStorage.tsx).
82	 *
83	 * It lives in this pure module for exactly the reason `walletSplit` does: the
84	 * client has to be able to import it, so what is shown is byte-for-byte what is
85	 * charged. Until 2026-07-27 the server computed
86	 * `Math.max(0, Math.round(monthlyCents * remainingMonths))` and AddStorage computed
87	 * the same expression over its OWN private copy of `MS_PER_AVG_MONTH` — the two
88	 * places agreeing by convention that this codebase has been bitten by repeatedly
89	 * (the wizard's promo line, the "+30 days" renew button, the resize picker before
90	 * it was moved onto lib/proration.ts). Pass `remainingMonths(expiresAt, now)` from
91	 * lib/proration.ts as the second argument; do not re-derive it.
92	 *
93	 * Clamped at both ends: an expired term (negative months) prorates to zero rather
94	 * than crediting, and a negative price can never come out as a negative charge.
95	 */
96	export function extraDiskProrateCents(monthlyCents: number, monthsRemaining: number): number {
97	  const monthly = Math.max(0, monthlyCents);
98	  const months = Math.max(0, monthsRemaining);
99	  if (!Number.isFinite(monthly) || !Number.isFinite(months)) return 0;
100	  return Math.max(0, Math.round(monthly * months));
101	}
102	
103	/** Is `gb` a purchasable amount (a positive multiple of the step, within range)? */
104	export function isValidExtraDiskAddGB(gb: number): boolean {
105	  return (
106	    Number.isInteger(gb) &&
107	    gb >= EXTRA_DISK_MIN_GB &&
108	    gb <= EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB &&
109	    gb % EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB === 0
110	  );
111	}
112	
113	/**
114	 * Coerce arbitrary input to a purchasable amount: rounded DOWN to the step and
115	 * clamped to [0, EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB]. Rounding DOWN (never up) means a
116	 * malformed value can only ever cost the customer less, never more. Returns 0
117	 * for "no extra disk", which every caller treats as a no-op.
118	 */
119	export function normalizeExtraDiskGB(gb: unknown): number {
120	  const n = Number(gb);
121	  if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n <= 0) return 0;
122	  const stepped = Math.floor(n / EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB) * EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB;
123	  if (stepped < EXTRA_DISK_MIN_GB) return 0;
124	  return Math.min(EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB, stepped);
125	}

127	/** Selectable amounts for the wizard/server-page controls: 10…500 GB by 10. */
128	export function extraDiskOptions(): number[] {
129	  const out: number[] = [];
130	  for (let g = EXTRA_DISK_MIN_GB; g <= EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB; g += EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB) out.push(g);
131	  return out;
132	}

135	 * The largest amount a server can still add without breaching the effective-disk
136	 * ceiling, rounded DOWN to the step. 0 means "already at the ceiling".
137	 */
138	export function maxAddableExtraDiskGB(planDiskGB: number, extraDiskGB: number): number {
139	  const headroom = EXTRA_DISK_MAX_TOTAL_GB - effectiveDiskGB(planDiskGB, extraDiskGB);
140	  if (headroom < EXTRA_DISK_MIN_GB) return 0;
141	  return Math.min(EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB, Math.floor(headroom / EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB) * EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB);
142	}

144	/** Human label for an extra-disk line item / notification. */
145	export function extraDiskLabel(gb: number): string {
146	  return `${Math.max(0, Math.round(gb))} GB extra disk storage`;
147	}

150	 * Clamp a raw "extra GB to add" input to a valid, on-step, in-range amount (0
151	 * allowed) — the SHARED-HOSTING order form's own normalizer. Rounds to the
152	 * NEAREST step (unlike `normalizeExtraDiskGB` above, which rounds DOWN for the
153	 * VPS disk-expand slider's "never cost more than shown" guarantee); hosting's
154	 * extra disk is chosen from a fixed set of stepped options, not typed free-form,
155	 * so nearest-step is the correct behaviour here and has always been.
156	 *
157	 * Lives in this plain module (not lib/actions-hosting.ts, which is a `"use
158	 * server"` file) so it can be imported by lib/actions-payment-providers.ts
159	 * (PayPal/Coinbase hosting-order creation) WITHOUT becoming a second
160	 * network-callable export of a Server Actions module — see
161	 * test/auth-lockouts.test.ts's "HAZARD" suite, which exists precisely to catch
162	 * a pure helper being exported from a `"use server"` file for no reason.
163	 */

165	  const n = Math.round((Number(raw) || 0) / EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB) * EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB;
166	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB, n));

 * phrasing the UI needs.

 *
 * The original incident: the button read `Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)` and
 * charged **$97.09**, moving the expiry twelve months — the label hardcoded
 * "+30 days" and the plan's MONTHLY price while `renewNow` charged a full term.
 * The fix was to compute the quote and the charge in one place.
 *
 * The second incident, hours later and in this very file: that shared place was
 * written as fresh arithmetic over `plan.priceCents`, which silently ignored
 * `gamePlan`. A game server carries BOTH a base `planId` and a `gamePlanId`, and
 * it is sold at the game plan's flat price — `minecraft-mm8w85` was sold at
 * $4.99 while its base Starter plan is $8.99. So the new shared quote would have
 * charged a game-server owner **80% more than they agreed to** the moment they

 * the automatic renewal sweep in `worker/billing.ts` already used it.

 * wrong formula, it was a SECOND formula. So there is exactly one, it lives in
 * `renewalCharge`, and everything that quotes or charges a renewal goes through
 * it — the worker sweep, the card path, this button, and the server page.
 */

  /** Total charged, in cents — tax-INCLUSIVE (net + tax) when a rate was passed. */
  totalCents: number;

  netCents: number;

  taxCents: number;

  taxRatePercent: number;

  months: number;
  /** Human label for the duration, e.g. "12 months" / "1 month". */
  durationLabel: string;
  /** What the customer is buying ("Starter VPS", or the game plan's name). */

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Icon } from "./Icon";

/**
 * Dark / light switch.
 *
 * Writes `data-theme` on <html> and remembers the choice in localStorage. The
 * FIRST paint is handled by an inline script in app/layout.tsx, not by this
 * component — a React effect runs after hydration, which is one paint too late
 * and shows a white flash on every load for anyone on light.
 *
 * Dark is the default and stays the product's identity; light is opt-in. The
 * rail and top bar are dark in both (see `.nx-dark-island` in globals.css), so
 * this control always sits on a dark surface and does not need to restyle
 * itself when the theme flips.
 */

export const THEME_KEY = "nx-theme";

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const [light, setLight] = useState(false);

  /* Read what the inline script already decided, rather than deciding again —
     two sources of truth here is how a toggle ends up out of step with the
     page it is toggling. */
  useEffect(() => {
    setLight(document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-theme") === "light");
  }, []);

  function toggle() {
    const next = !light;
    setLight(next);
    const root = document.documentElement;
    if (next) root.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    else root.removeAttribute("data-theme");
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(THEME_KEY, next ? "light" : "dark");
    } catch {
      /* Private mode or blocked storage. The theme still applies for this
         session; it just will not be remembered, which is the right failure. */
    }
  }

## What I built

## The combined-checkout question (point 5) — resolved as option (b), and why

I did **not** build a combined PaymentIntent. Two verified facts made that the wrong call, not just the cheap one:

1. `resizeServer`, `expandServerDisk` and `purchaseDedicatedIp` each **queue a Job**, and each refuses to start while any job is `QUEUED`/`RUNNING` on that server (`pending > 0` guard in all three). The platform's "one in-flight job per server" rule means that even behind one PaymentIntent, **the backend physically cannot apply them together**.
2. Each has its own Stripe session creator (`createResizeCheckout` / `createDiskExpandCheckout` / `createDedicatedIpCheckout`), its own metadata and its own idempotent confirm/webhook fulfilment. `upgradeServerBackupTier` has **no card leg at all** — wallet only. A combined intent would therefore take money for changes it could not yet apply and reconcile them later across four fulfilment paths: paying for something not yet done, which is the exact failure the money comments in `lib/actions-disk.ts` / `lib/wallet-split.ts` exist to prevent.

So the cart shows the combined picture (real, computed through the same functions the server charges through) and applies the changes **in order through the existing actions, one confirmation each**. The sheet says this out loud: *"Each change is its own operation and this server runs one at a time, so we apply them in the order above and you confirm payment once per change. Nothing is charged for a change until that change is accepted."* Per-item wallet/card splits are computed against a **running** balance, because summing one `walletSplit` of the combined total would display a number nobody is ever charged. Items that succeed are reported back and cleared from the selection.

**Capability gap for the user to decide on later:** a genuinely combined charge needs a backend that can hold several *pending changes* against one payment and drain them as jobs free up — a pending-change queue plus a new confirm path. That doesn't exist today and is a real backend project, not a UI change.
